options.systemMessage:
You are a real estate agent writing a personalised re-engagement email sequence to a cold lead about a specific property.

Generate exactly 5 emails. Each must have a distinctly different angle and tone, following this strategy:

Email 1 — Warm Re-engagement:
Acknowledge their previous interest warmly.
Reference the specific property.
2 sentences max body. Low pressure — just reconnecting.

Email 2 — Value Add (Day 4):
Share a useful insight about the property or local market.
Frame as genuinely helpful — position agent as advisor.
Not a sales pitch.

Email 3 — Social Proof (Day 8):
Mention without names that similar buyers have been 
active in this area or property type recently.
Create gentle urgency without being pushy.

Email 4 — Direct Ask (Day 14):
Straightforward — are they still interested?
Short and direct. One question only.
Make it easy to reply yes or no.

Email 5 — Breakup Message (Day 21):
Warm final message — closing the loop.
Leave the door open for future contact.
No pressure — wish them well.

RULES:
- Never mention AI or automation
- Always sound personally written by the agent
- Reference the property address specifically in each email
- Reference the lead name naturally
- Body 2-3 sentences maximum each
- Format each email_body as two parts separated by \n\n:
  Part 1: Greeting line only, e.g., "Hi Sarah,"
  Part 2: Message body as one paragraph

Output ONLY a valid JSON array of exactly 5 objects.
No preamble, no markdown, no text outside the array:
[
  {
    "touch": 1,
    "email_subject": "subject line",
    "email_body": "Hi {name},\n\nBody here."
  }
]

You are a real estate assistant classifying a reply from a lead in a re-engagement email sequence.

Classify the reply as exactly one of:
- Hot: Lead expresses genuine interest, wants to proceed, asks questions, or suggests a meeting
- Neutral: Acknowledging but non-committal — asking for more time, general questions, or vague responses
- Unsubscribe: Lead wants to be removed from contact, expresses disinterest, or asks to stop emails

Output ONLY valid JSON, no preamble, no markdown:
{
  "sentiment": "Hot | Neutral | Unsubscribe",
  "reasoning": "one sentence explanation",
  "summary": "one sentence summary of what the lead said"
}

nodes.name: Gmail: Apply Drip Label to Touch

parameters.content:
## AI Property Drip Campaign — Multi-Step Nurture Sequence

Re-engages cold leads with a personalised five-touch email sequence over 21 days — each email referencing a specific property and automatically tailored to a different angle and tone.

### How it works
A lead is added to the sequence via webhook. Gemini pre-generates all five emails in one call — warm re-engagement, value-add, social proof, direct ask, and a breakup message. Touch 1 sends immediately. 
Touches 2–5 send automatically on Days 4, 8, 14, and 21. If the lead replies at any point, the sequence stops, the reply is classified as Hot, Neutral, or Unsubscribe, and the agent is notified instantly. Every morning a digest summarises all active sequences.

### Requirements
- **Gmail** OAuth2 — all emails
- **Gemini** API key — email pre-generation + reply sentiment classification
- **Google Sheets** OAuth2 — sequence state + daily digest log

### Setup
1. Connect Gmail, Gemini, and Google Sheets credentials.
2. Create the Drip Campaign Manager sheet template — three tabs: Active Sequences, Sequence Log, Daily Digest Log.
3. Create a Gmail label named **drip-sequence**.
4. Update AGENT_NAME and AGENT_EMAIL in the Sequence Configuration node.
5. Section C has its own Configuration node — keep both in sync.

### Customization
- Adjust wait days between touches in the Sequence Configuration node.
- Edit the Gemini prompt to change tone, length, or language of the generated emails.
- Add a lead manually via webhook or by flagging a row in Google Sheets.
- Stop any sequence manually by setting Status = Stopped in the Active Sequences sheet.

## *Section A*
## Viewing Request Entry
Webhook is the default. It accepts a POST from any source, including pervious templates from QualMatic. Google Sheets trigger is optional — the agent flags a lead directly in the Active Sequences sheet. Both triggers feed into Normalize Lead Details which maps both formats into clean named fields.

## Configuration & Pre-Generation
All sequence settings live in the Configuration node. One Gemini call pre-generates all five emails upfront. Parse & Store Email Content parses the returned JSON array and extracts each subject and body into named fields ready for Sheets storage.

## Sequence Creation & Touch 1
All five pre-generated emails are written to the Active Sequences sheet in one Append Row operation. Touch 1 sends immediately. The drip-sequence Gmail label is applied to the sent email so replies are detectable. Thread ID is stored in Sheets — used later to match replies to the correct sequence.

## Wait, Check & Send (Touches 2–5)
Each iteration waits the configured days, fetches the current sequence status from Sheets, and checks whether it still matches the expected status. If a lead has replied or the agent stopped the  sequence, the IF node exits the loop cleanly. Build Touch Email HTML formats the pre-stored body before Gmail sends — label applied after each send.

## Daily Digest: Delivery & History
An IF node skips sending on days with no active or responded sequences — no empty emails. Gmail sends the digest to the agent. Every digest is logged to the Daily Digest Log tab with counts for active, completed, and responded sequences.

## *Section C*
## Daily Digest: Fetch & Build
Schedule trigger fires at 8am. Section C Configuration node sets agent email for delivery. Fetch All Sequences reads every row from Active Sequences. Build Daily Digest groups them by status — active, responded, and completed — and formats the summary HTML email.

## *Section B*
## Reply Detection: Incoming Message Filter
Gmail Trigger watches the drip-sequence label every minute. An IF node filters out sent messages — only genuine replies with INBOX label pass through. The reply thread is fetched via Google API and Extract Latest Reply pulls the most recent message body, stripping the quoted original email text.

## Sentiment Classification & Sequence Match
Gemini classifies the reply as Hot, Neutral, or Unsubscribe. Parse Sentiment extracts the sender email and reply text for downstream matching. Match Sequence to Reply finds the active sequence by Thread ID stored in Sheets. Status updates to Responded and the agent receives an instant notification with sentiment and the reply text.

## Notify & Log
If a sequence is found, update the status to Responded, and the agent receives an instant notification with the sentiment and reply text. Finally, log the sequence to a Google Sheet.

##  Preparing the Touch Loop
Prepare Remaining Touches outputs four items — one per remaining touch — each carrying its wait days, email content, and status transitions. Split In Batches processes one touch at a time so each Wait → Check → Send cycle completes fully before the next touch begins.

## Gmail Label Required
Create a label named drip-sequence in Gmail before activating this workflow. Gmail → Settings → Labels → Create new label. This label must match GMAIL_LABEL in the Configuration node exactly.

## Wait Node Testing
Wait nodes are set to Days for production.
For local testing change the Wait node to 
1 minute to verify the full sequence fires.
Change back to Days before submitting or 
activating for real leads.

## Update Configuration Before Activating
Set AGENT_NAME and AGENT_EMAIL before first use.
Section C has its own Configuration node. 
Update both nodes to keep settings in sync.
Wait days between touches can be adjusted here, 
SEQUENCE_DAYS_2 through SEQUENCE_DAYS_5.
